sections.html:
Spokane is the seat of Spokane County, on the Spokane River in eastern Washington, less than 20 miles from the Idaho line. It had 230,783 residents in July 2025, second in the state after Seattle. Fewer city households own their homes than in the county as a whole, so a good share of Spokane houses are rentals when they sell. The 2020 to 2024 numbers for the city and the county:

Housing measureSpokane citySpokane County
Typical home value, owner-occupied$363,500$410,700
Owner-occupied housing rate58.8%64.5%
Median gross rent$1,215$1,283
Households97,446218,395

The school district over a parcel shifts its levy. Spokane Public Schools covers most of the city, and Mead takes the north county beyond the city limits. Pull the parcel record before you quote anybody a number.

sections.h2: Who bills property tax for a Spokane house?
sections.html:
City Hall sends nothing. Property tax in Spokane is billed and collected by the Spokane County Treasurer, with values set by the county Assessor. The City of Spokane is one of roughly 56 taxing districts in the county that hand their budgets to the Assessor each November.

The city's share goes mainly into the General Fund for police, fire, streets, parks and the library. Its proposed 2025 to 2026 budget assumed the 1% increase allowed on regular levies, and it carries a streets levy and a public safety personnel levy fund as dedicated revenue. Other lines on the statement belong to the county, the school district, the state schools and whatever special district covers the lot.

Water, sewer and trash service are paid by fees, not property tax. Before you close, ask the city utility billing office whether the address has an unpaid utility balance.

  • Treasurer's counter: 1116 W. Broadway Ave. in the county courthouse, open weekdays from 8:30 a.m. until 4 p.m. Phone 509-477-4713.
  • Assessor: 509-477-3698.
  • For checks in the mail, use the Treasurer's post office box, number 199, zip 99210.

Payment comes in a spring half and a fall half, on April 30 and October 31. Small bills, those under $50, come due all at once in April. A date falling on a Saturday, Sunday or county holiday rolls to the next working day. With this fall's half behind you, the next deadline is April 30, 2027.

One statement a year arrives with two coupons. No statement by March 31? Call 509-477-4713 or search SCOUT, the county's online lookup. Escrow customers should check with the lender, because the Treasurer neither bills mortgage companies nor tracks them.

The courthouse has two drop boxes, and they take checks only. Ahead of each deadline the Treasurer sets up outside collection days, two Fridays and two Tuesdays, at Spokane Valley City Hall and the North Spokane Library. Envelopes are judged by federal postmark. Postmarks have been slipping after postal changes, so mail early.

Interest starts May 1 for a missed first half and November 1 for a missed second half, and it runs on the full year's amount. Houses and small residential buildings of up to four units carry 0.75% a month and never a penalty. Other property is charged 1% a month and then takes a 3% penalty on June 1 and 8% on December 1.

State law lets the Treasurer set up payment agreements and accept partial payments on current and past-due taxes, with money going to the oldest year first (RCW 84.56.020). After the death of a spouse, parent or stepparent, a hardship waiver is possible if you give notice within 60 days of the due date (RCW 84.56.025). Interest cannot be waived when the statement went to an address supplied by the taxpayer or the taxpayer's agent, a closing agent for example.

If your bank bounces a payment, add a $30 fee on top of interest, penalty and costs.

sections.h2: How do you challenge a Spokane assessment?
sections.html:
Appeals for a house inside city limits go to the Spokane County Board of Equalization. Use the petition form and file it by July 1 of the assessment year. If your Change of Value Notice was mailed later, you get 30 days from that mailing. Filing costs nothing. Calling or writing a letter does not replace the form.

The board looks only at market value, and the assessor's number is presumed right unless your evidence is clear, cogent and convincing (RCW 84.40.0301). Build your case around these points:

  • Tax amount, percentage increase, other properties' values and personal hardship cannot be considered.
  • Comparable sales close to January 1 of the assessment year make the strongest case.
  • Supporting papers must arrive seven business days before you appear.
  • Notice of the hearing comes 15 business days ahead.

Call the Assessor first at 509-477-3698, since many disagreements end in a stipulated value. Lose at the county level and the State Board of Tax Appeals is next, with 30 calendar days to file. The county revalues every parcel each year and inspects each one at least once in six years.

Seniors and people retired because of disability can apply for a property tax exemption through the Spokane County Assessor at 509-477-3698. Senate Bill 6162, signed after the 2026 session, changes the income limits starting in 2027, so ask for the limits that apply to you instead of trusting older numbers.

Every statement is required by RCW 84.56.020 to point to the exemption and the deferral program. An owner who is income-qualified, lives in the home and faces a tax foreclosure action can have interest and penalties waived about three years after delinquency, once per property.

Buyers get a special path too. Someone who bought between July 1 and December 31 of the assessment year for under 90% of assessed value can ask the Board of Equalization to reconvene after the normal deadline.

sections.h2: What should you do about back taxes when selling in Spokane?
sections.html:
Get a payoff letter from the Treasurer that covers each unpaid year, pass it to the closing agent, and check that the agent holds the right parcel number and mailing address. Remember that interest stays in place if the county's statement was mailed to an address the closing agent supplied.

Excise tax on the sale is its own charge, owed to the county treasurer at the moment of sale, and the seller usually covers it. For sales from January 1, 2027, a house at the city's $363,500 median value falls entirely in the 1.1% state bracket, before any local rate is added.

Waiting is risky. At three years past delinquency, the treasurer is required to begin foreclosure by certificate of delinquency (RCW 84.64.050).

sections.h2: Closing checklist for a Spokane seller
sections.html:
A tidy tax file makes a sale move faster. Start a few weeks before you list and work down this list:

  • Pull the parcel record on SCOUT and write down the parcel number, the school district and what each half shows as paid.
  • Ring 509-477-4713 for a written payoff when any earlier year is open.
  • Ask the city utility billing office about any water, sewer or trash balance on the address.
  • Tell the Assessor at 509-477-3698 if a senior or disability exemption or a deferral is attached, so the closing agent knows to plan for it.
  • Give the closing agent a mailing address you actually check, because late-notice mail goes to whatever address is on file.

A cash buyer can often close quickly, and no lender runs its own tax review. The payoff letter is still needed, since any back tax comes out of your proceeds.

faqs.q: Where does my Spokane property tax payment go?
faqs.a: To the Spokane County Treasurer, in person on W. Broadway Ave., by mail to P.O. Box 199, or online. The phone is 509-477-4713. City Hall collects none of it.

faqs.q: When is Spokane property tax due?
faqs.a: Twice a year, April 30 and October 31. Under $50 is paid in one lump in April. Next up is April 30, 2027, shifting to the next business day if it is a weekend.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Spokane property value?
faqs.a: Your appeal goes to the county's equalization board, and the cutoff is July 1, or a month after the value notice went out if that comes later. No fee applies, and you will want market evidence such as nearby sales.

faqs.q: What interest applies to late Spokane property tax?
faqs.a: A house of up to four units pays 0.75% monthly with no penalty. Other property pays 1% monthly and also takes the June and December penalties. Each charge is figured on the whole year's tax.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Spokane house that owes back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Whatever is owed gets paid by escrow out of your sale money. Get the payoff from the Spokane County Treasurer and give your closing agent the right parcel number and mailing address.
